title: Test a fair coin after every flip
hook: A 5% test flags a fair coin 1 time in 20. Does checking after every flip change that?

knows: a result outside the 5% level happens by chance about 1 time in 20 (p-values)
doesNotKnow: that repeated looks give noise many chances to cross the line
that a fixed-sample test assumes a single look

misconception: If the test is run at the 5% level, stopping early when it first looks significant is still at the 5% level.
objective: The learner can say that testing after every flip and stopping at the first significant result wrongly flags a fair coin about 29% of the time, against about 6% for a single look at the end.
keyState: Look-every-flip and look-only-at-the-end both shown on 20 lines, then all 100 seeded fair coins counted: 23 flagged by peeking, 5 by the end-only look.

claims.text: The test calls a coin biased when |heads - tails| / sqrt(flips) is above 1.96 (the 5% level under the normal approximation).
claims.source: Standard z-test with the normal approximation; BAND = 1.96 in model.ts. It is an approximation for small flip counts.

claims.text: Testing after every flip from flip 10 to flip 100 and stopping at the first significant result wrongly flags a fair coin 28.5% of the time.
claims.source: Exact dynamic programme over the +-1 walk (exact().peek = 0.2854), removing mass at the first n in 10..100 with |d|/sqrt(n) > 1.96; recomputed in node.

claims.text: A single look at flip 100 wrongly flags a fair coin 5.7% of the time.
claims.source: P(|2H - 100| / 10 > 1.96) = P(H >= 60) + P(H <= 40) = 0.0569 (exact().end). Not 5% because the walk only takes steps of 2 at n = 100.

claims.text: In the 100 seeded fair coins on the stage, 23 left the band at some look from flip 10, and 5 were outside it at flip 100.
claims.source: Experiment i uses mulberry32(6000 + i), untuned (first seed tried). Over 300 other seed sets of 100 coins, peeking flagged 28.3 on average (range 15 to 40) and the end-only look 5.8 (range 0 to 13). The first 20 lines shown flag 6 (every look) and 0 (end only).

claims.text: Each extra look gives noise another chance to cross the line, so the more often you look, the more often a fair coin is wrongly flagged.
claims.source: Follows from claims 2 and 3: 28.5% against 5.7%. The 1.96 rule assumes a single planned look (see Armitage, McPherson & Rowe (1969), J. Royal Statistical Society A 132: 235-244, to be checked).

recall.question: You check a fair coin's test result after every flip and stop the first time it looks biased at the 5% level. Compared with checking once at the end, wrong 'biased' calls are
recall.why: Every look is another chance for noise to cross the line: about 29% of fair coins get flagged with checks at flips 10 to 100, against about 6% for one look.
